basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 42.' and it opens 'VERS. 42.-- Dixitque Rebecca ad Jacob: Audivi, quod frater tuus Esau minatur occidere te.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text:
VERS. 42.-- Dixitque Rebecca ad Jacob: Audivi, quod frater tuus Esau minatur occidere te. Q aeritur quomodo annuntiata sunt verba Esau Rebeccae, quibus comminatus est occidere fratrem suum; cum Scriptura dicat hoc cum in sua cogitatione dixisse? Nisi quia hic nobis datur intelligere quod divinitus ei [Z., eis] revelabantur omnia.
